proven: Native service keeps one normal batch and delivery path while independently polling stop messages during core I/O.
Lookahead uses the same sender/chat, trusted principal binding and current group consent; it does not admit, deliver or advance Telegram offsets.
Core stop is bound to the exact pending turn and can precede its ingress, preventing the early-start race.
One stop request is durably bound to its original target and cannot be reapplied to a later turn after restart.
Temporary lookahead errors retry within the loop without restarting normal processing.
Tests block A and B, show only A stopped, and subsequently deliver skipped middle/stop messages through the ordinary path.

fixedFindings: Per-active deduplication could apply one stop to A and B; now persistent per-command target plus worker deduplication.
Lookahead network failure could exit the control loop; now retries in loop.

limits: Synthetic Telegram provider; no real Telegram user messages sent.
An already admitted provider call can complete after stop; this does not kill in-flight remote work.
/turns/stop shares the existing trusted internal connector boundary with /turns/respond; not an independent public-browser authorization API.
Latest changes are not in preliminary image728df94; final candidate rebuild and full release gate remain required.
Task-wide execution bound still to be assessed.
